stories.title: McKinsey (Oct 9, 2026): CPG Companies Are Using Agentic AI to Cut Costs When They Should Be Using It to Recapture Growth
stories.body: McKinsey's October 9, 2026 article argues that CPG businesses are leaving growth on the table because most deployments of agentic AI are focused on cost reduction and accelerating existing work rather than top-line recovery. The article notes that investors in CPG companies reward top-line growth more than margin expansion, and that the real opportunity lies in the increasingly complex CPG–retailer relationship. In performance management specifically, McKinsey finds AI can track KPIs, detect variances, and recommend actions while cutting the human effort required by roughly half — freeing commercial teams to act on growth opportunities rather than reporting.
stories.why: McKinsey naming the 'cost-only' AI deployment as the wrong strategy is a gift for an enterprise retail-AI sales team: it validates that the market is stuck in efficiency pilots and has not yet wired agents into commercial growth workflows. Graas can position its context and data layer as the prerequisite that lets CPG commercial teams move from variance-reporting agents to revenue-recovery agents.

stories.title: SAP Launches Joule Agents Across Supply Chain at SAP Connect 2026, Grounded in SAP Knowledge Graph
stories.body: At SAP Connect on October 6–8, 2026, SAP made its Autonomous Enterprise architecture generally available, deploying Joule Work and 50 domain-specific Joule Assistants across finance, procurement, HR, and supply chain — with new agents specifically targeting supply chain planning, warehousing, outbound optimization, fulfillment, and transportation dispatching. The agents are architecturally grounded in the SAP Knowledge Graph, which maps more than 7 million data fields to provide reliable business context, plus customer-specific process logic and approval workflows stored in HANA Cloud. SAP's Q3 2026 earnings simultaneously crossed €10 billion in quarterly revenue for the first time, with cloud backlog growing 28% to €24.1 billion, which SAP CEO Christian Klein attributed to agentic AI deployment as a distinct demand driver — not merely an ERP migration feature.
stories.why: SAP's explicit architecture decision — agents must be grounded in a governed knowledge graph before they can touch live ERP data — is the strongest enterprise proof point available that context infrastructure is table stakes, not a nice-to-have. For Graas, this is the anchor case that shows retail and CPG buyers what 'agent-ready' ERP looks like, and surfaces the gap for customers not yet on that foundation.

stories.title: BCG Survey (Oct 21, 2026): 68% of Retailers Expect Agentic Commerce to Be Significant or Transformational Within Two Years — But Most Haven't Rewired Their Data
stories.body: BCG's October 21, 2026 survey of 150 retailers and brands finds that 68% expect agentic commerce to have a significant or transformational effect within two years, and that eight in ten retailers have already taken a position on external AI agents — with 42% making their data discoverable by any agent, 32% giving access only to chosen agents, and 6% blocking agents entirely. BCG argues retailers must now win two games simultaneously: the direct shopper visit and the external agent's recommendation, which place fundamentally different demands on loyalty programs, retail media, and personalization infrastructure. Traditional growth levers like banner ads and sponsored search are expected to slow as discovery moves off retailers' own websites and into agent-mediated flows.
stories.why: The BCG finding that only 42% of retailers have made their data machine-readable to any agent — while 68% expect agentic commerce to be transformational — defines the exact gap Graas addresses. A salesperson can use this to show retail and CPG prospects that the strategy decision is already being made by their competitors, while the data readiness work has barely started.

stories.title: BCG and Futurum Data: AI Now Consumes 17% of IT Budgets, Non-AI SaaS Licenses Being Cut to Fund It — and Gartner Warns 40%+ of Agentic Projects Will Be Canceled by 2027
stories.body: BCG's 2026 CIO survey finds AI's share of IT budgets has more than tripled, from 5% to 17%, with server prices running 80% above 2025 rates and CIOs now required to tie every AI dollar to measurable business value. Futurum's concurrent 2H 2026 CIO survey finds that 36.4% of organizations that reallocated funds to cover AI overruns did so by cutting non-AI software licenses, while 27.5% of buyers expect to purchase fewer core SaaS seats as their use of vendors' AI features grows. Gartner's positioning, cited in multiple analyst notes, calls 2026 a 'trough of disillusionment' year and expects more than 40% of agentic AI projects to be canceled by end of 2027 absent proven ROI.
stories.why: The budget squeeze is the forcing function for every enterprise AI conversation in late 2026: CIOs are cutting point-solution SaaS to fund agents, but Gartner warns that 40%+ of agentic projects will be canceled if they can't prove ROI. Graas can use this to reframe its pitch — a governed context and data layer is not an added cost, it is what separates the 60% of projects that survive from the 40% that get cut.
